methodological_eligibility.evidence_quote: the PG2E solution comes into play upstream, facilitating the initial identification of a relevant scope for deploying an EMS. It thus constitutes a strategic preparatory tool

stage1.ineligibility_reason: Presents PG2E, a combinatorial-optimization software tool that selects which municipal buildings form the ISO 50001 certification scope. It ranks candidate subsets with simple aggregate statistics (mean consumption, upper quartile) as proxies for obsolescence/regulatory status; it does not present, propose, evaluate, or critique an EnPI/EnB measurement model (no baseline, no normalisation of energy against driver variables). Authors explicitly place PG2E upstream of ISO 50006 EnPI-based energy-performance measurement. Tool/software design without EnPI/EnB measurement-model content.

paper_type.evidence_quote: PG2E is an innovative, fully digital solution that uses a combinatorial approach to automatically identify the ISO 50001 certification scope

stage1.notes: Case study: French municipality Quesnoy-sur-Deule, 2021 electricity data for 15 buildings (public/institutional). 'Energy consumption per m2' appears once as one of seven correlation variables but is not adopted; chosen criteria are mean and Q75 for subset selection. Judged ineligible as scope-selection software rather than an EnPI/EnB model; borderline noted for human review.
